_plates.caption: Li Kenong before a cave dwelling in Yan'an. He served as a member of the Central Special Branch, as deputy director and then director of the Central Social Affairs Department, and as director of the Central Intelligence Department.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white group photo of four men in suits and ties standing outdoors before foliage.
_plates.caption: Pan Hannian, Liu Shaowen, Wu Kejian and Liu Renshou, photographed together in 1949. From left: Liu Shaowen, who served as intelligence chief of the Southern Bureau and of the Military Commission; Pan Hannian, who headed the Central Special Branch and served as deputy director of the Central Social Affairs Department; Liu Renshou, who served as a secret intelligence agent and adviser to the United Front Work Department of the Shanghai Municipal Committee; and Wu Kejian, who headed intelligence for the CCP Nanjing Bureau and served as director of the United Front Work Department of the East China Bureau.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white group photo of four men in Communist-army uniforms and caps standing in a row in front of a building.
_plates.caption: Luo Ruiqing (second from left), Yang Qiqing (third from left), Wu Lie and Zou Yan, photographed together in 1949. Luo Ruiqing served as director of the Security Bureau of the First Front Army and as Minister of Public Security of the People's Republic of China. Yang Qiqing served as chief of the Anti-Traitor Department of the Eighth Route Army's forward headquarters and as deputy Minister of Public Security. Wu Lie served as commander of the Central Guard Regiment and commander of the Beijing Garrison. Zou Yan served as political commissar of the Security Regiment of the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region and as deputy political commissar of the Shenyang Military Region.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of a young man in a soft cap and army tunic, turned and looking up to the side.
_plates.caption: Zeng Xisheng, who took up intelligence work as early as the Red Army period and decrypted a great volume of Nationalist military intelligence.

_plates.alt: Grainy black-and-white photo of a man in a light tunic standing, hand on hip, before a tree.
_plates.caption: Wu Defeng in 1938 at the secret intelligence station's base in Caojia Lane, Xi'an. He served as director of the Central Liaison Bureau and as chief of the Xi'an intelligence station.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of a man in a long gown and skullcap standing with a cane beside a brick gateway with a latticed window.
_plates.caption: Wang Chaobei, who carried out intelligence work in Xi'an under the cover of a merchant's identity.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of two men in army uniforms and caps standing before a stone-stepped doorway.
_plates.caption: Zhou Xing (right), director of the Border Region Security Office, with his deputy Du Liqing [Xu Jianguo], in Yan'an.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a man in rimless glasses and a collarless jacket, looking slightly to the side.
_plates.caption: The "Red Sherlock Holmes," Bu Lu, in Yan'an.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of a man in a suit seated cross-legged on a rattan chair in a plant-filled room.
_plates.caption: Qian Zhuangfei, who in 1929 penetrated the entourage of Xu Enzeng, head of the Nationalist Zhongtong, serving as his secretary; one of the "Three Heroes of Longtan."

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of a smiling young man in an open-collared shirt holding up a revolver.
_plates.caption: Xiong Xianghui, who in 1941 penetrated Hu Zongnan's Nationalist command, serving as Hu Zongnan's secretary; one of the "Latter Three Heroes."

_plates.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a balding man in round glasses and a suit and tie.
_plates.caption: Yan Baohang, a secret CCP intelligence agent who had been a senior aide to Zhang Xueliang and who successfully obtained strategic intelligence including the date of Germany's attack on the Soviet Union.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a young man in a light suit and dark tie.
_plates.caption: Yan Youwen, a secret CCP member who served as Fu Zuoyi's personal secretary and as deputy director of the office of the North China "Bandit Suppression Headquarters."

_plates.alt: Black-and-white group photo of three men standing outdoors, two in shirtsleeves and one in a dark suit.
_plates.caption: In 1941, Nakanishi Ko, Nishizato Tatsuo and Ozaki Shotaro (from left), photographed in Shanghai. These Japanese-national intelligence agents supplied the CCP with vital intelligence during the War of Resistance Against Japan and were the first to sound the alarm of the coming Pacific War.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of a man in a suit seated beside a young child.
_plates.caption: Ozaki Hotsumi and his daughter Yoko, who was born in Shanghai.

_plates.alt: Grainy black-and-white portrait of a young man in round glasses and a buttoned tunic.
_plates.caption: Zheng Wendao, a CCP intelligence agent, named in the first roster of renowned martyrs and heroic groups of the War of Resistance Against Japan published by China's Ministry of Civil Affairs in 2014.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of a woman in a dark cheongsam leaning against a railing in a room.
_plates.caption: Shen Anna, who penetrated the Confidential Office of the Nationalist Central Party Headquarters as a confidential stenographer and repeatedly obtained important intelligence.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white oval-framed portrait of a smiling woman with wavy hair.
_plates.caption: Guan Lu, who penetrated the magazine Nusheng (Women's Voice), jointly run by the Japanese Consulate in Shanghai and the press bureau (intelligence bureau) of the Japanese naval marines.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a young woman with a bobbed hairstyle, smiling.
_plates.caption: Zhang Luping, who in 1939 established a secret Party branch at the heart of the Juntong intelligence apparatus.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a young person in glasses and a high-collared garment.
_plates.caption: Xiao Minghua, a CCP member, who was martyred in Taiwan in 1950 at the age of 28.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a man in a peaked military cap and decorated dress uniform.
_plates.caption: Han Liancheng, the "Invisible General" who lay concealed at Chiang Kai-shek's side.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white portrait of a young man in round glasses, a light jacket and dark tie.
_plates.caption: Li Bai, the model for the character Li Xia in the film The Eternal Wave, who long ran a clandestine radio station in Shanghai. On the eve of Shanghai's liberation he was secretly murdered by Nationalist agents.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white full-length photo of a man in a light suit standing before a dark backdrop.
_plates.caption: Lieutenant General Wu Shi, working undercover in Taipei in 1949.

_plates.alt: Blurred black-and-white photo of a woman in the foreground with two uniformed men behind her.
_plates.caption: Zhu Feng, a CCP member and Wu Shi's liaison, who was executed in Taiwan on 10 June 1950.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white group photo of eight elderly people, four seated women in front and four men standing behind, indoors.
_plates.caption: Some trainees of the first session of the Qilipu Reconnaissance and Intelligence Training Class of the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region Security Office, photographed together in 1999. Front row, from left: Yang Yuying, once deputy secretary of the Party Committee of the Ministry of Public Security, wife of Zhou Xing; Lu Huang, once a cadre of the All-China Women's Federation, wife of Bu Lu; Zhuo Lin, once an adviser to the General Office of the Central Military Commission, wife of Deng Xiaoping; Jiang Peng, once a division chief of the Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau, wife of Tan Zhengwen. Back row, from left: Xie Heng, once an adviser to the Ministry of Public Security; Zou Yu, once Minister of Justice; Liu Ping, once a bureau chief of the Third Department of the General Staff; Yang Huanglin, once a bureau chief of the Ministry of Light Industry.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of three people, a woman and two men, seated together indoors.
_plates.caption: Li Qiming and Li Ning, photographed with the author of this book in 1995. Li Qiming (center) served as deputy director of the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region Security Office, director of the Northwest Public Security Bureau, governor of Shaanxi Province, and executive secretary of the Yunnan Provincial Party Committee. Li Ning (left) served as a staff member of the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region Security Office and as head of the International Liaison Department of the Yunnan Provincial Party Committee.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of two men seated side by side on a sofa before a potted plant.
_plates.caption: Luo Qingchang (right), photographed with the author of this book in 2003. Luo Qingchang served as director of the First Office of the CCP Central Social Affairs Department and as director of the CCP Central Investigation Department.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white group photo of four people standing together, an elderly man at center flanked by others.
_plates.caption: Wang Dongxing, photographed with the author of this book in 1995. Wang Dongxing (second from left) served as director of the Second Office of the CCP Central Social Affairs Department and as director of the Central Security Bureau. At far left is Wang Dongxing's wife, Yao Xiang'e. Yang Yuying (third from left), wife of Zhou Xing, served as a cadre of the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region Security Office and as deputy secretary of the Party Committee of the Ministry of Public Security.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of two older men seated side by side before a wall hung with calligraphy.
_plates.caption: Shi Jinqian (left), photographed with the author of this book in 1996. Shi Jinqian served as director of the Security Department of the General Political Department, as deputy director of the General Political Department of the People's Liberation Army, and as head of the Army-wide Political and Legal Affairs Group.

_plates.alt: Color-toned photo of two older men seated together indoors, an electric fan behind them.
_plates.caption: On 20 June 2014, Zhang Zhongru (left) photographed with the author of this book. Zhang Zhongru served as director of the Intelligence Department of the General Staff of the People's Liberation Army.

_plates.alt: Black-and-white photo of two men seated facing each other in a room whose shelves hold small ornaments.
_plates.caption: Ling Yun (right), photographed with the author of this book in 1998. Ling Yun served as a staff member of the Central Social Affairs Department, as deputy Minister of Public Security, and as Minister of State Security.

_plates.alt: Color-toned photo of two men seated in armchairs conversing in a furnished room.
_plates.caption: Yang Side (right), photographed with the author of this book in 2009. Yang Side served as director of the Liaison Department of the Political Department of the 13th Column of the East China Field Army and as director of the Liaison Department of the General Political Department.

_plates.alt: Color-toned photo of three people standing together outdoors on a street.
_plates.caption: Zou Yu (center), photographed with the author of this book. Zou Yu served as chief of the Secretariat Section of the Border Region Security Office and as Minister of Justice.

_plates.alt: Color-toned photo of two men standing together before a wall of bookshelves.
_plates.caption: Cai Cheng (left), photographed with the author of this book. Cai Cheng served as a secretary of the Border Region Security Office and as Minister of Justice.

_plates.alt: Color ID-style photo of a man in a green dress military uniform with ribbon bars, against an orange background.
_plates.caption: The author, Hao Zaijin.
